More Flour Here
Half Million
Bags Arrive
From America

Shanghai's flour supply was greatly replenished yesterday by the arrival of nearly 400,000 bags of American flour aboard the s.s. Suzan V. Luckenbach, a U.S. registered vessel.

Due early next week will be another 250,000 bags of flour from America which will be brought here by the s.s. American Star, also a U.S. Registered vessel.

Both ships embark for Shanghai from Seattle early last month. They will also bring other U.S. cargo to this city.

Agents for the Suzan V. Luckenbach are Lacey and Cannon, a British concern, while agents for American Star are the Mollers' Ltd.

Meanwhile, the cheap sale of flour here, sponsored by the S.M.C., continued with flour supplied to the Council by the Fou Foong Flour Mill.

更多面粉抵沪
五十万袋
自美运抵

昨日，随着美国注册船只“苏珊·V·卢肯巴赫”号（s.s. Suzan V. Luckenbach）抵达，载有近 40 万袋美国面粉，上海的面粉供应得到极大补充。

预计下周初，另一批 25 万袋来自美国的面粉将由同样为美国注册船只的“美国之星”号（s.s. American Star）运抵此处。

两艘船均于上月初从西雅图启程前往上海。它们还将为本市带来其他美国货物。

“苏珊·V·卢肯巴赫”号的代理人为英商 Lacey and Cannon 公司，而“美国之星”号的代理人则为 Molliers' Ltd.（音译）。

与此同时，由工部局（S.M.C.）资助的面粉廉价销售活动仍在继续，所需面粉由福丰面粉厂供给工部局。

Flour And Wheat
As outport dealers were not in the
market yesterday on lower Tientsin quota-
tions trading in native flour practically
came to a standstill. The unofficial rates
remained unchanged, and only a slight
turnover was reported. The mills supplied
7,500 bags to local retail shops at $10.30
per bag.
Buying interest in native wheat nar-
rowed down yesterday as dealers adopted
an awaiting attitude. As a result the
Foch Sing flour mill bought three car-
loads of Soochow wheat at $24.75 per bag.

面粉与小麦

由于外地商人昨日未因天津报价较低而入市交易，国产面粉的交易几乎陷入停滞。非官方汇率保持不变，据报道成交量仅略有增加。各面粉厂以每袋 10.30 美元的价格向本地零售店供应了 7,500 袋面粉。

昨日，由于商人采取观望态度，对国产小麦的购买兴趣减弱。因此，福兴面粉厂以每袋 24.75 美元的价格购买了三车皮苏州小麦。

S.M.C. Thanks Two
Flour Mills Here
Placed Large Quantities
Of Flour at Disposal of
Public at Low Prices
In identical letters addressed to the
managers of the Fou Foong and Foh
Sing Flour Mills the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council has recorded its appre-
ciation of efforts made by the mills
during the past year in making avail-
able large quantities of flour for pub-
lic sale at reasonable prices. The
public it was stated, greatly benefit-
ted as a result of the action of the
mills.
In its letter the Council expressed
the hope that the mills concerned
will continue to sell flour at moder-
ate prices as long as it is possible
for them to do so.
In a communique issued yesterday
on the flour situation the Council
stated that as the actual daily re-
quirements of consumers in the Set-
tlement and French Concession are
8,318 bags, the authorities have found
it necessary to allot the full require-
ments daily excepting Wednesdays
and Sundays when no deliveries will
be made to consumers.
The Foh Sing Mill sold 5,000 bags
and the Fou Foong Mill 1,059 bags
of flour on January 31, and February
1, making it possible to meet the
full requirements of consumers on
Wednesday of this week, leaving a
balance of 3,800 bags for future
needs. If 4,518 bags can be accumul-
ated by a deduction of ten per cent.
from imported foreign flour corres-
ponding to local No. 2 grade which
has arrived here since the beginning
of the year, a full day's supply to
consumers on Wednesday of next
week can also be met by supplying
this amount of foreign flour and 3,800
bags of local flour, the communique
added.

工部局感谢本地两家面粉厂
以低价向公众提供大量面粉

上海公共租界工部局在向福丰面粉厂和福兴面粉厂经理发出的内容相同的信函中，记录了对这两家面粉厂在过去一年中努力以合理价格向公众提供大量面粉出售的感激之情。信中指出，公众因面粉厂的此举而大大受益。

工部局在信中表示，希望有关面粉厂在力所能及的情况下，继续以适中价格出售面粉。

在昨日发布的关于面粉局势的公告中，工部局指出，由于租界和法租界消费者的实际每日需求量为 8,318 袋，当局认为有必要每日分配全部需求量，但星期三和星期日除外，这两天不向消费者交货。

福兴面粉厂在 1 月 31 日和 2 月 1 日售出了 5,000 袋面粉，福丰面粉厂售出了 1,059 袋，这使得本周三能够满足消费者的全部需求，并剩余 3,800 袋以备未来之需。公告补充道，如果从今年年初至今抵达的、相当于本地二级品的进口外国面粉中扣除百分之十，能积累起 4,518 袋面粉，那么通过供应这批外国面粉和 3,800 袋本地面粉，也可以满足下周三消费者一整天的需求。

CHEAP FLOUR SALE
BEING CONTINUED

Two Mills Will Supply
6,932 Bags Daily;
Thanked By S.M.C.

Effective from last Monday, the
Foh Sing Flour Mill is supplying
5,875 bags of flour daily to con-
sumers in the Settlement and
French Concession, except on Sun-
days, at a price of $23 per bag plus
the customary 30 cents per bag
commission to flour dealers. The
Fou Foong Flour Mill will similarly
supply 1,059 bags of flour, making a
daily total from the two mills named
of 6,932 bags of flour.
Since the actual daily require-
ments of consumers in the Settle-
ment and French Concession are
8,318 bags, the Authorities have
found it necessary to allot the full
requirements daily except on Wed-
nesdays and Sundays, on which days
no deliveries will be made to con-
sumers.
As the Foh Sing Mill sold 5,000
bags and the Fou Foong Mill 1,059
of flour on January 31 and again on
February 1, it will be possible to
meet the full requirements of con-
sumers on Wednesday of this week,
leaving in hand a balance of 3,800
bags for future needs. If 4,518 bags
of flour can be accumulated by de-
duction of 10 per cent. from import-
ed foreign flour corresponding to
local No. 2 Grade, which has arrived
in Shanghai since the beginning of
1941, a full day's supply to con-
sumers on Wednesday of next week
can also be met by supplying this
amount of foreign flour and 3,800
bags of local flour.

Letter Of Appreciation
The following letter has been ad-
dressed by the Municipal Council to
the General Managers of the Fou
Foong and Foh Sing Flour Mills—
"The Council desires to place on
record its grateful appreciation of
your Company's efforts in making
available throughout the past year
large quantities of flour which were
sold at reasonable prices to actual
consumers in Shanghai who greatly
benefitted thereby. The Council
earnestly hopes that you will kindly
agree in the public interest to con-
tinue to sell flour at moderate prices
as long as it is possible for you to
do so."

廉价面粉销售
仍在继续

两家面粉厂将每日供应
6,932 袋；
获工部局致谢

自上周一生效，福兴面粉厂除星期日外，每日向租界和法租界的消费者供应 5,875 袋面粉，价格为每袋 23 美元，另加给面粉商人的惯例佣金每袋 30 美分。福丰面粉厂也将同样供应 1,059 袋面粉，使得上述两家面粉厂的每日总供应量达到 6,932 袋。

由于租界和法租界消费者的实际每日需求量为 8,318 袋，当局认为有必要每日分配全部需求量，但星期三和星期日除外，这两天不向消费者交货。

鉴于福兴面粉厂在 1 月 31 日和 2 月 1 日分别售出 5,000 袋面粉，福丰面粉厂售出 1,059 袋，本周三将能够满足消费者的全部需求，手头剩余 3,800 袋以备未来之需。如果能从 1941 年初以来抵达上海的、相当于本地二级品的进口外国面粉中扣除 10%，积累起 4,518 袋面粉，那么通过供应这批外国面粉和 3,800 袋本地面粉，也可以满足下周三消费者一整天的需求。

感谢信

以下是工部局致福丰和福兴面粉厂总经理的信函——

“工部局谨记录对贵公司 efforts 的衷心感谢，贵公司在过去一年中提供了大量面粉，以合理价格出售给上海的实际消费者，使他们大大受益。工部局恳切希望贵公司出于公共利益考虑，同意在力所能及的情况下，继续以适中价格出售面粉。”

MAR 1 1940
Tientsin Starts Flour Control
BRITISH MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
（印：BRITISH MUNICIPAL COUNCIL TIENTSIN）
EMERGENCY ORDER NO. 11
CONTROL OF FLOUR
(1) All persons (which term together with the terms 'no person' or "any person" shall include all firms, companies, institutions and combinations of persons of any description whatsoever) in the British Municipal Area who are:
(a) Importers of flour, and
(b) Flour merchants other than as importers of flour,
shall forthwith register with the Secretary and Engineer, British Municipal Council. Such registration shall be accompanied by a return specifying the quantity and brand of any flour held at the date hereof by such person registering and the place of storage thereof and be otherwise sufficient to enable the Council to register flour stocks and establish such control as in the opinion of the Council may be necessary in the public interest. Such registration is required to be effected forthwith.
(2) The Council may from time to time issue regulations hereunder approved by H.M. Consul-General or form any Committee for the better control of the matters hereby referred to. Any such regulations shall be of the same effect as this Order.
(3) Any persons infringing this Order or any regulation hereunder shall be liable to a fine not exceeding $500 (Five hundred dollars) and to have his stocks placed under direct control of the Council.
(4) The term "the Council" herein contained shall include any committee of the Council appointed hereunder.
A. E. TIPPER,
CHAIRMAN.
COUNCIL ROOM,
TIENTSIN, February 24, 1940.
APPROVED:
OSWALD WHITE,
H.B.M. CONSUL-GENERAL

1940 年 3 月 1 日
天津开始实施面粉管制
英国工部局
（印：天津英国工部局）
紧急命令第 11 号
面粉管制
(1) 在英国工部局辖区内，所有人员（该术语以及“无人”或“任何人”等术语应包括任何性质的所有商号、公司、机构和个人组合），若属于以下类别：
(a) 面粉进口商，以及
(b) 除作为面粉进口商以外的面粉商人，
应立即向英国工部局秘书兼工程师登记。此类登记应附有一份申报表，说明登记人在此日期持有的任何面粉的数量和品牌及其储存地点，并以其他方式充分使工部局能够登记面粉库存并建立工部局认为符合公共利益所需的此类管制。此项登记需立即办理。
(2) 工部局可不定期发布经英王陛下总领事批准的规章，或成立任何委员会以更好地管制此处提及的事项。任何此类规章应与本命令具有同等效力。
(3) 任何违反本命令或据此发布的规章的人员，将被处以不超过 500 美元（五百美元）的罚款，并将其库存置于工部局的直接管制之下。
(4) 此处包含的“工部局”一词应包括据此任命的工部局任何委员会。
A. E. TIPPER,
主席。
会议室，
天津，1940 年 2 月 24 日。
批准：
OSWALD WHITE,
英王陛下总领事
（批：D G 3/4 (1/3) 归档）

Move To Halt
Hoarding Taken

British Area Ordering
Stock Registration
With Council

More municipal experiments in
controlling the price of foodstuffs
are seen in an emergency order
issued by the British Municipal
Council in Tientsin for ascertaining stocks of flour, and in the
fixing of the price of this at
PRB$14 per bag, as stated in a
private telegram received in
Shanghai today from the north-
ern city.

Food prices were fixed in the
Tientsin French Concession weeks
ago, as announced by the Shang-
hai Evening Post at the time.
The FMC in Shanghai has in the
past few days decided to control
prices, and now the Shanghai
Municipal Council has appointed
a sub-committee to see how the
Settlement can do the same thing.
Members of the sub-committee
are Messrs. J. Filtere, jr. (chair-
man of the American Association
of Shanghai), Frithjof Hoehnke
and W. Mellor (director of
Messrs. A. R. Burkill & Sons).

Success of the Tientsin move
regarding flour is regarded as
doubtful by Shanghai merchants,
as the selling price reported to be
fixed (equivalent of Shanghai
$12) is over Shanghai $4 below
present replacement costs, and
that therefore imports of flour
into Tientsin will cease.

Control of prices in the Shang-
hai French Concession, when it
comes into effect, is also con-
sidered not likely to cause great
reductions in every line of every
line of everyday commodities. It
is held, however, that it will pre-
vent any sudden soaring of prices
in the event of sudden falls of
exchange, for instance.

Many local merchants are op-
posed to "governmental" control
of prices in that it is an inter-
ference with the laws of econo-
mics. They point out that if
prices are fixed at lower than re-
placement costs, the commodities
concerned will not be replaced.
page_data.zh:
采取遏制
囤积行动

英租界下令
向工部局
登记库存

天津英国工部局发布了一项紧急命令，旨在查明面粉库存并将价格定为每袋伪币 14 元，正如今天从北方城市收到的一份私人电报所述，这被视为控制食品价格的更多市政实验之一。

正如《上海晚邮报》当时宣布的那样，天津法租界数周前已固定食品价格。上海法公董局（FMC）在最近几天决定管制价格，现在上海公共租界工部局已任命一个小组委员会，研究租界如何也能做同样的事情。小组成员包括 J. Filtere, jr. 先生（上海美国人协会主席）、Frithjof Hoehnke 先生和 W. Mellor 先生（A. R. Burkill & Sons 公司董事）。

上海商人认为天津方面关于面粉的举措能否成功尚存疑问，因为据报道固定的售价（相当于上海货币 12 元）比目前的补货成本低 4 元以上，因此进入天津的面粉进口将会停止。

上海法租界的价格管制一旦生效，也被认为不太可能导致各类日常消费品价格的大幅下降。然而，人们认为，这将防止在汇率突然下跌等情况下价格突然飙升。

许多本地商人反对“政府”管制价格，认为这是对经济规律的干涉。他们指出，如果价格固定在低于补货成本的水平，相关商品将无法得到补充。

National Herald :-

THEFT FROM RICE SHOPS IN POOTUNG

Many cases of thefts from rice shops have occurred in Pootung. On February 19 several rice shops at Hu Ka Moo Kiao (胡家木桥) were victimized. Post duty puppet policemen and Japanese soldiers did nothing although they saw the thefts. Rice shops in Pootung now close their doors and only leave a small opening to do business.

Chinese-American Daily News publishes the following letter received from one Ho Liang (何亮) :-

THE CAUSES FOR THE HIGH PRICES OF DAILY NECESSITIES

According to reports from reliable sources, the following are the causes for the sharp increases in the prices of rice, flour and coal briquettes in Shanghai and it is to be hoped that the authorities will take severe measures against such activities:-
(1) The principal element responsible for the manipulation of rice is the proprietor of the - Chong Rice (-昌) located at ---Bridge. He works in conspiracy with the - Chong - Rice Shop (-昌-) at the corner of ---- Road. He was responsible for the sharp increases in the prices of rice taking place after the withdrawal of Chinese forces from Shanghai in the winter of 1937. His activities were slightly checked after the issue of the joint proclamation by the two Municipal Councils but soon afterwards he entered into conspiracy with a foreign concern---- & Company and instigated it to enhance the price of foreign rice as a deterrent to joint purchases so as to enable the price of Chinese rice to go up.
(2) As regards flour, the - Kee Shop (-记) on North -- Road is at the back of the rising tendency in the price of this commodity. Realizing that Dairen is short of supplies of this class of goods, the shop has ordered large consignments amounting to 350,000 bags of flour from various local leading flour mills, at a price of $4.30 to $4.50 per bag. As a result of this order the flour mills have been rendered short of deliveries for ordinary consumers, thereby resulting in a continued increase in the price. This affords a very good opportunity to make more profits. 《国民日报》：

浦东米店遭窃

浦东发生多起米店被盗案件。2 月 19 日，胡家木桥的几家米店受害。站岗的伪警察和日本士兵虽然目睹了盗窃行为，却未采取任何行动。目前，浦东的米店紧闭大门，只留一个小口做生意。

《中美日报》刊登了一封来自何亮（Ho Liang）的来信：

日用品价格上涨的原因

据可靠消息来源报道，上海大米、面粉和煤球价格急剧上涨的原因如下，希望当局对此类活动采取严厉措施：
(1) 操纵大米的主要元素是位于---桥的-昌米行（- Chong Rice (-昌)）老板。他与----路拐角处的-昌-米店（- Chong - Rice Shop (-昌-)）勾结。他应对 1937 年冬季中国军队撤离上海后发生的大米价格急剧上涨负责。在两工部局联合发布公告后，他的活动受到轻微遏制，但不久后他便与一家外商----公司勾结，唆使其提高洋米价格，以阻碍联合采购，从而使华米价格得以上涨。
(2) 关于面粉，北--路的-记店（- Kee Shop (-记)）是这种商品价格上升趋势的背后推手。该店意识到大连此类货物供应短缺，便以每袋 4.30 至 4.50 美元的价格，向本地各家主要面粉厂订购了大量货物，总计 35 万袋面粉。由于这一订单，面粉厂无法向普通消费者交货，从而导致价格持续上涨。这提供了赚取更多利润的绝佳机会。由于不便大量处置其采购货物，且为了掩盖其活动不被公众知晓，该店已开始以略低的价格进行廉价销售

货物价格降至每担2.80或2.90美元以进行竞争。
大茂厂因余先生（Mr. Yu）的请求而开始此次销售，但发现
自己无法与其他商家竞争。
结果，煤球价格开始飙升至
每担4美元以上。最近，本地报刊刊登广告称，已为公众
订购了此类货物20,000多吨。实际上，这不过
是一种欺骗公众的烟幕弹。

（编者注：从写信人处收到的信件中包含了所有对米、面粉和
煤球价格进行操纵的商号的完整名称和地址。本报在出版时特意省略了这些信息，希望相关商号能
尽快醒悟。鉴于此事关系到当地数百万居民的
生计以及该地区的和平与秩序，我们请求
当地公共团体要求各家工厂和
商行停止交付向其订购的货物，并将其
供应给广大公众消费者，以便稳定商品
价格。）

page_data.en:
Flour And Wheat

While local flour mills sold 7,500 bags
of second-grade products to retail shops
at $10.30 per bag, the unofficial market
ruled rather dull with total sales to North
China and South Sea dealers amounting
to 2,000 bags.
The market for native wheat ruled
steady yesterday with local dealers buying
one carload of Soochow wheat at $27.00
per bag while the Fooh Sing and the
Fou Foong flour mills were not in the
market.

面粉与小麦

10.30美元的价格向零售店出售了7,500袋
二等品，但非官方市场
相当清淡，销往华北和

page_data.en:
FEB 2 . '10

'RE-SELLERS OF CHEAP
FLOUR ARRESTED

Fraudulent Activities
Fail To Escape Sharp
Eyes Of Detectives

Vigilant Chinese detectives yes-
terday arrested 15 persons who
were found to have resold bags of
flour which they had obtained from
the equitable-sales-of-flour service.
These vagrants were spotted in the
vicinity of the Jui Chi Flour Store,
32 North Chekiang Road, which is
one of the largest distributing cen-
tres of cheap flour.

More than 1,000 poor people had
been waiting in front of the flour
store even before daybreak. Many
of these people had flocked to the
place on the previous evening, and
had stayed on the sidewalk over-
night.

Owing to adequate police super-
vision, order remained good dur-
ing the distributing hours in spite
of the unusually large crowd. But
a few detectives were also on the
spot. They followed some suspic-
ious buyers after they had got their
bag of flour, and discovered that
many of them then started bar-
gaining with some prospective buy-
ers. The re-sale price as agreed
by both parties in these cases rang-
ed from $13 to $14. The detectives
placed both buyers and re-sellers
under arrest, a total of 15 persons.

It was learnt that the 15 will be
sent to court for hearing this morn-
ing.

1910年2月2日

“倒卖廉价
面粉者被捕”

欺诈活动
未能逃过
警探锐利目光

警觉的中国警探昨日
逮捕了15人，这些人被发现
转售了他们从平价面粉供应服务中
获得的面粉袋。这些流浪汉在
浙江北路32号瑞记面粉店附近
被盯上，该店是
廉价面粉最大的分销中心
之一。

早在黎明前，就有
1,000多名穷人在面粉店前
等候。其中许多人于
前一天晚上涌向此地，并
在人行道上过夜。

由于警方监管得力，尽管
人群异常庞大，但在分发
期间秩序保持良好。但也
有几名警探在现场。他们
跟随一些可疑买家在拿到
一袋面粉后，发现他们中的许多人
随后开始与一些潜在买家
讨价还价。在这些案例中，双方
商定的转售价格在
13至14美元之间。警探将
买家和转售者均予以逮捕，共计
15人。

据悉，这15人将于今晨
被送交法庭审理。

Whilst millions of local residents are experiencing
difficulties in maintaining a living due to the high cost

CAROLINA EVENING POST & MERCURY
JAN 7 / 1940

Japanese Grab Wheat
For Seized Mills

Chinese Using
Reserve Stock

Flour Price Restricted
Despite High Cost
Of Replacement

Still using their reserve stocks of wheat as Japanese are seizing as much of the grain as possible, Shanghai millers have been able to sell wheat around $10.25 to $10.50 a bag recently, although this would not be possible with new purchases of higher-priced grain.

Japanese interests are acquiring Chinese wheat for use in the mills which they have seized in their "Sino - Japanese cooperation" scheme, and little is going on the general market.

Poor Quality

Chinese wheat, poor in quality, is now priced at $17 per new picul (50 kilograms), and as it takes a picul and a quarter to make two bags of flour, the production cost of one bag would be $11½, or higher than the sale price of wheat made from reserve stocks.

Thanks to high freights and general rise in costs due to the European war, flour milled locally from foreign wheat would work out at a cost of $12.50 a bag.

Seized From Chinese

Mills used by the Japanese to grind the diverted wheat are those which they seized from private Chinese interests during their invasion of the country.

While technically referring to the present management of these mills as an example of "Sino-Japanese cooperation," the procedure has been for the Japanese to seize the mills and subsequently make an offer to the rightful owners to come in with them, so as to make it appear as if they were cooperating. In case of refusal, the Japanese have seized the mills entirely.

《卡罗来纳晚邮报与水星报》
1940年1月7日

日本人夺取小麦
供被占面粉厂使用

中国人使用
储备库存

尽管替换成本高企
面粉价格仍受限制

由于日本人尽可能多地夺取谷物，上海面粉厂一直使用其小麦储备库存，因此最近能够以每袋约10.25至10.50美元的价格出售小麦，尽管如果是购买高价新粮则不可能做到这一点。

日本利益方正在获取中国小麦，用于其在“中日合作”计划中夺取的面粉厂，流入一般市场的很少。

质量低劣

质量较差的中国小麦目前定价为新担（50公斤）17美元，由于制作两袋面粉需要一担又四分之一的小麦，因此每袋面粉的生产成本将为11.5美元，高于由储备库存制成的小麦售价。

得益于高运费和因欧洲战争导致的总体成本上升，用外国小麦在当地磨制的面粉成本将达到每袋12.50美元。

从中国人手中夺取

日本人用来磨制被转移小麦的面粉厂，是他们在侵华期间从中国私人利益方手中夺取的。

虽然在技术上将这些面粉厂的当前管理称为“中日合作”的范例，但其程序是日本先夺取面粉厂，随后向合法所有者提出加入合作的提议，以制造合作的假象。如果遭到拒绝，日本人便完全夺取面粉厂。

CHINA PRESS.
JAN 1 C 1910

Soaring Flour Price Seen
As Stocks Are Depleted

Because the Japanese are alleged-
ly seizing all the wheat they can,
the price of the grain will tend
to increase in the near future, it
was predicted yesterday. Local
millers were still selling wheat at
$18.50 a picul, it was reported. This
level could not be maintained ac-
cording to local merchants for when
present stocks give out, new pur-
chases of higher-priced grain will
have to be made.
The same report stated that, in
the name of "Sino-Japanese Co-
operation," the Japanese were tak-
ing over Chinese mills and offering
the legitimate owners a business
partnership. If this "co-operation"
was withheld, the Japanese were
said to have seized the mills al-
together.
The Japanese system then was
to use these seized mills to grind
confiscated stocks of wheat, the re-
port continued. Much of these
stocks were said to have been seiz-
ed from private Chinese sources
during the Nipponese invasion of
China.
The high freights and the rise in
prices due to the European war
have raised the price of foreign
flour to $11.00 per bag, it was stat-
ed.

January 15, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Central China Daily News :-

RISING PRICE OF NOODLES

After the enforcement of a limit on the
price of rice, rice speculators, without consideration for
the livelihood of the poor people, turned their attention
to flour, thereby causing an upward tendency in the price
of flour. At the end of last week, the price of flour
exceeded $10 a bag. This has caused a further rise of

After the outbreak of hostilities, the price

At a joint meeting of the noodle dealers held last Friday,
it was decided to increase the price to $0.20 per catty
with effect from January 15, 1940.
Poor people have been living more on noodles
than rice due to the high price of rice and they will be
faced with more difficulties due to the price of noodles
being three times as high.

SHANGHAI TIMES.

JAN 1 7 1940

LARGE INCREASE IN
PRICE OF FLOUR

40 Catties Bag Costs
$12.50 As Compared
With $8 Last Year

Following the recent sharp ad-
vance in the price of rice, the
price of wheat flour as quoted in
the local foodstuff stores, hit a
new peak yesterday, aggravating
the already miserable situation of
the masses of Shanghai who de-
pend upon a fixed salary for their
living. Only three weeks ago flour
was sold a little over $8 a bag of
40 catties, but yesterday it ad-
vanced to the high price of $12.50
a bag.

One year ago wheat flour was
sold at some $4 a bag. This price
remained rather stable until last
June, so that only seven months
ago it was still sold about $4. In
the course of these seven months,
the price of this second staple
food has trebled.

The problem of high flour price
is no less serious than that of rice
price, because a sizable portion of
the population, especially people
from North China, use flour as
daily food instead of rice. Norm-
ally, and customarily, the price of
flour should be one quarter of
that of rice. That is, four bags
of flour should equal to one sack
of rice containing 160 catties, in
price. With the best quality of
rice now selling at $40, flour is
selling much higher than rice in
proportion. Thus far, there has
been no price limit prescribed on
flour by public authorities.

《上海泰晤士报》。

1940年1月17日

面粉价格
大幅上涨

40斤装每袋成本
12.50美元，而去年为8美元

继近期大米价格急剧上涨之后，
本地食品店报价的小麦面粉价格昨日
创下新高，加剧了依靠固定薪水
生活的上海大众的悲惨处境。仅在三周前，
40斤装的面粉售价略高于8美元，但昨日已
涨至每袋12.50美元的高价。

一年前，小麦面粉售价约为每袋
4美元。这一价格一直保持相对稳定，直到去年
六月，因此仅在七个月前，售价仍约为
4美元。在这七个月里，这种第二主食
的价格翻了三倍。

面粉高价问题并不比大米价格问题
轻微，因为相当一部分人口，尤其是来自
华北的人们，日常食用面粉而非大米。通常
和习惯上，面粉价格应为大米价格的
四分之一。也就是说，四袋面粉的价格应等于
一袋含160斤的大米。目前最优质的大米
售价为40美元，按比例计算，面粉售价远高于大米。
迄今为止，公共当局尚未对面粉规定
限价。

AUG 22 1933

Flour And Wheat

On account of the rice shortage, most
of the local consumers took flour instead
of rice during the last few days, so that

by the mills on account of a brisk demand
shown by local retail shops. The selling
rate moved up to $6.20, or $0.20 high
compared with last week-end's final rate.
The total sales of second-grade product
for local dealers amounted at 20,000 bags.
With a shortage of flour for local
supplies, the mills refused to accept the
orders from the outport dealers. The
South Sea operators also requested some
flour for Hongkong and Amoy, but did
not receive any offers from the mills.
The selling rate of native wheat was
further high in yesterday's market, al-
though the market has received a con-
siderable amount of wheat from the
interior. The mills were interested in
absorbing during the last few days. There-
fore, the rate was increased by $0.30 per
bag according to the market record. The

was noted at $9.70 per bag, and the Poo-

1933年8月22日

面粉与小麦

由于大米短缺，在过去几天里，大多数本地消费者改用面粉代替大米，因此鉴于本地零售店表现出的旺盛需求，面粉厂提高了国产面粉的售价。售价涨至6.20美元，比上周末的最终收盘价高出0.20美元。面向本地经销商的二等品总销量达到2万袋。
由于本地供应的面粉短缺，面粉厂拒绝接受外埠商人的订单。南洋运营商也为香港和厦门求购一些面粉，但未从面粉厂获得任何报价。
昨日市场上国产小麦售价进一步走高，尽管市场已收到来自内地的大量小麦。面粉厂在过去几天里一直有兴趣吸纳货源。因此，根据市场记录，价格每袋上涨了0.30美元。新收获的贵甸（Kwei Tien，音译）国产小麦报价为每袋9.70美元，而浦东小麦售价为8.85美元，是市场上的最低价。

2381A/S/C

SHANGHAI TIMES.

AUG 21 1939

Irate Crowd
Storms Into
Flour Shop

Robs Changping Rd. Shop
Of 100 Bags Of Flour;
Premises Wrecked

Knowing that there was a considerable quantity of flour stored in the premises, a mob of Chinese at 8 o'clock last night stormed the rice and flour shop of Yi Yue Sing, at 81 Changping Road, near Markham Road. The crowd tore into the shop, smashing the big front window, and forcibly gained entrance by one stepping over the other. Part of the crowd escaped with 100 bags of flour and $30 in cash was also stolen from the wrecked premises

The mob were in a state of frenzy, spurred on by agitation that the shop was hoarding the flour and that a serious shortage was expected soon when the shops would sell only at high prices, it was reported. On attacking the shop, the mob simply overpowered the employees, while everyone that could lifted a bag of flour to his shoulder and stepped on the other man in getting out. The violent action of the mob in the rather small premises soon tore the place up.

Police Disperse Mob

A riot squad from the Gordon Road district were soon dispatched to the scene and effectively dispersed the mob, who scattered in all directions upon the police arrival. Four of the rioters were arrested and taken to the police station, from where they will most likely be brought up for trial today. None of the flour was recovered as it appears that certain groups had been designated to take off with the flour while others stormed and crowded the premises.

Many rice and flour shops are taking extra precautions to prevent their premises from being looted, as rumours are going the rounds among local rice dealers that disturbances are likely to be created by angry Chinese unable to pay the increasing costs of rice and flour and that there may be a possible shortage of this necessity of life.

(批：Liu 6/8)
page_data.zh:
2381A/S/C

《上海泰晤士报》。

1939年8月21日

愤怒人群
冲进
面粉店

抢劫昌平路店铺
100袋面粉；
场所被毁

得知该场所内储存有大量面粉后，昨晚8时，一群中国人冲进了位于马克姆路（Markham Road，今黄陂北路附近）附近的昌平路81号“益裕兴”（Yi Yue Sing，音译）米面店。人群撕开店铺入口，砸碎巨大的前窗，并踩着彼此的身体强行进入。部分人群带着100袋面粉逃离，并从被毁坏的场所中偷走了30美元现金。

据报道，这群暴徒处于疯狂状态，受到煽动，称该店囤积面粉，且预计很快会出现严重短缺，届时商店只会高价出售。在袭击店铺时，暴徒轻易制服了店员，而每个能动手的人都扛起一袋面粉，踩着其他人逃出去。暴徒在相当狭小的场所内的暴力行为很快将地方弄得一片狼藉。

警方驱散人群

戈登路（Gordon Road，今江宁路）警区的一支防暴队很快被派往现场，有效驱散了人群，警察到达后人群四散奔逃。四名暴徒被捕并被带到警察局，他们很可能今天将被提审。由于似乎有特定群体负责带走面粉，而其他人则冲击并拥挤在场所内，因此没有追回任何面粉。

许多米面店正在采取额外预防措施，以防止其场所被抢劫，因为本地米商中流传着谣言，称因无法支付日益上涨的大米和面粉成本而愤怒的中国人可能会制造骚乱，且这种生活必需品可能会出现短缺。

（批注：Liu 6/8）

page_data.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,
23831
AUG 21 1939

Chinese Mob Raids
Flour Shop
100 Bags Stolen by Crowd.
Of 500 After Destroying
Front of Shop

In the first serious food riot to have occurred in Shanghai in the past two years, an angry mob of about 500 Chinese rushed a rice and flour shop at 81 Changping Road shortly after 8 p.m. yesterday, almost completely wrecked the frontage of the shop and managed to get away with approximately 100 bags of flour. A police party arriving at the scene was able to arrest three men and a woman who were about to run away with 14 bags of flour.
The exact cause for the affair is still being investigated but it was presumed that a number of professional agitators were responsible for the incident while bystanders profited by the occasion in stealing all the flour which they were able to lay their hands on.

Precautions Planned
An alarm was sent into Gordon Road police station 10 minutes after the riot had started and when a police party consisting of a foreign detective, a Chinese detective and a Chinese constable arrived on the scene, the mob dispersed which in the opinion of observers, indicates that agents provocateurs were responsible for the affair, as the support of the mob ceased with the arrival on the scene of the three police officers.
As a result, it was understood last night that the Settlement police are to take precautions similar to those in force during the rice shortage in August and September 1937 when, it will be recalled, all rice shops inside the foreign areas were given police protection after a number of riots had occurred following the decision of the rice dealers that only limited quantities of rice would be sold to each customer.
In last night's affair, it was understood that the mob not only took the flour but also some $30 which was found in one of the drawers of the counter. It is not known why the attack was made on this particular shop; but the theory that revenge may have been responsible is being entertained by investigating detectives.
The four arrested persons were understood to have been members of the mob and were not believed to have been agitators. The extent of the damage caused by the riot could not be ascertained last night but it is believed to have been considerable.
page_data.zh:
《北华捷报》，
23831
1939年8月21日

中国暴徒突袭
面粉店
人群在摧毁店铺门面后
偷走100袋面粉中的
500人参与

这是过去两年来上海发生的首起严重食物骚乱，昨晚8点后不久，约500名愤怒的中国暴徒冲进了昌平路81号的一家米面店，几乎完全毁坏了店铺的门面，并成功带走了大约100袋面粉。赶到现场的警察逮捕了三名男子和一名妇女，他们正企图携带14袋面粉逃跑。
事件的确切原因仍在调查中，但据推测，一些职业煽动者对此事件负有责任，而旁观者则趁机偷走了所有他们能到手的面粉。

计划采取预防措施

骚乱开始10分钟后，警报被发送至戈登路警察局，当由一名外籍侦探、一名华籍侦探和一名华籍巡捕组成的警察队伍到达现场时，人群解散。观察人士认为，这表明挑衅者是事件的幕后黑手，因为随着这三名警官到达现场，人群的支持便停止了。
因此，昨晚获悉，租界警方将采取类似于1937年8月和9月大米短缺期间实施的预防措施。回想起来，当时在大米商人决定每位顾客只能购买限量大米后，发生了一系列骚乱，随后外国区域内的所有米店都获得了警方保护。
在昨晚的事件中，据悉暴徒不仅拿走了面粉，还拿走了在柜台其中一个抽屉里发现的约30美元。目前尚不清楚为何袭击这家特定店铺；但调查侦探正在考虑报复可能是起因的理论。
据悉，这四名被捕人员是暴徒成员，不被认为是煽动者。昨晚无法确定骚乱造成的损坏程度，但据信相当严重。

1939年8月6日

面粉与小麦

由于外埠商人热衷于购货运往天津、山东、广州和厦门，过去几天国产面粉售价不规则地走高，昨日市场上二等产品的价格进一步涨至8.30美元，较前一日最终价格高出0.10美元。本节所有经营者都积极参与，以最高价吸纳白米。

由于法币汇率低迷导致进口小麦价格高企，且各面粉厂库存有限，故拒绝接受外埠商人的订单。本地及内地商人在市场中占据主导地位，购买了30,000袋此类面粉，而外埠商人在整个交易节中仅零星吸纳。

由于进口小麦价格高昂，国产小麦的售价再次每袋上涨0.20美元，但中国面粉厂继续购入以补充库存。佛信面粉厂（Fosh Sing）和福丰面粉厂（Fou Foong）均以6.55至7美元的价格购买了5卡车新收获的南京、芜湖和泰阳（Taiyang，音译）国产小麦，而本地买家以6.55至7.30美元的价格吸纳了6卡车国产小麦。

CHINA PRESS
AUG 5 1939

Flour And Wheat

The selling price of native flour was irregularly high in yesterday's market, because a keen demand was made by the outport and local buyers. Satisfactory business was done in the session. The South Sea merchants were greatly interested in buying for transportation to Canton and Amoy, while the North China dealers took an active part in the market, as well as the local and the interior buyers who were willing to buy at the above price.
Owing to lack in the stock, the mills refused to sell their goods at ordinary rate at $5 per bag, and the price of second-grade product moved up by $0.20 per bag for local dealers to be paid in cash. The rate for outport dealers was increased to $5.20 in order cheque, because of the higher rate of discount on order cheque. The total sales in the day were estimated at 40,000 bags of different kinds of second-grade product. The local dealers and the interior traders bought 10,000 bags of this flour, and another 30,000 bags were absorbed by both North China and South Sea operators.
The price of newly-harvested native wheat was again high for selling, while the Chinese mills dominated in the market and asked large amounts of wheat for stocks. As a result, the rate moved up by $0.20 per bag. The Fooh Sing Flour Mills and Fou Foong Flour Mills bought 18 trucks of Soochow and Nanking newly-harvested native wheat, while the local dealers absorbed 9 trucks of this wheat.

1939年8月5日

面粉与小麦

昨日市场上国产面粉售价不规则地走高，原因是外埠和本地买家需求旺盛。本节交易情况良好。南洋商人对购货运往广州和厦门兴趣浓厚，而华北商人以及愿意以高价购买的本地和内地买家也积极参与市场。
由于库存不足，各面粉厂拒绝以每袋5美元的常规价格出售货物，二等产品的价格每袋上涨0.20美元，要求本地买家支付现金。由于订单支票贴现率较高，外埠商人的价格上调至5.20美元（凭订单支票支付）。当日各类二等产品的总销量估计为40,000袋。本地商人和内地贸易商购买了10,000袋此类面粉，另有30,000袋被华北和南洋经营者吸纳。
新收国产小麦的售价再次高企，中国面粉厂在市场占据主导，大量求购小麦以充实库存。因此，价格每袋上涨0.20美元。佛信面粉厂（Fooh Sing Flour Mills）和福丰面粉厂（Fou Foong Flour Mills）购买了18卡车苏州和南京的新收国产小麦，而本地商人吸纳了9卡车此类小麦。

AUG 4 1939

Flour And Wheat

A favorable trading in native flour was
witnessed in the market, and a large
amount of flour was sold to both local
and the outport dealers, while the out-
port dealers dominated in yesterday's bu-
siness. But the North China dealers were
greatly interested in buying, and asked
the mills to quote the price for outport
dealers according to the rate of discount
on order cheque. The mills therefore
announced the rate for outport buyers
at $6 per bag, and paid in order cheque.
Both the local and the interior traders
took an active part in buying for stocks,
during the high rate of white rice. The
selling rate for the above dealers remained
unchanged at $5 in cash per bag for
second-grade product. The total turnover
in the day amounted to 30,000 bags of
different kinds of native flour.
A fresh improvement in native wheat
was seen in the market yesterday, and
the selling rate was kept steady by the
holders, because the demand was brisk by
the dealers in the session, and many
Chinese mills were asked for a con-
siderable amount for stocks. As a result,
the rate moved up by $0.05 to $0.10, above
the last closing rate. There were large
shipments of newly-harvested native
wheat arrived in port from the growing
centers in the interior.
Both, the Fooh Sing and Fou Foong
Flour Mills, bought 6 trucks of Wushih,
Wuhu native wheat at from $6.60 to $6.70
per bag while the local dealers absorbed
11 trucks of Nanking, Quinsan and Soo-
chow newly-harvested native wheat at
$7.08.

1939年8月4日

面粉与小麦

市场上国产面粉交易有利可图，大量面粉售予本地和外埠商人，而外埠商人在昨日交易中占据主导地位。但华北商人购货兴趣浓厚，要求各面粉厂根据订单支票的贴现率向外埠商人报价。因此，各面粉厂宣布外埠买家的价格为每袋6美元，凭订单支票支付。在白米价格高企期间，本地和内地贸易商积极购入以充实库存。上述经销商的售价保持不变，二等产品为每袋现金5美元。当日总成交量为各类国产面粉30,000袋。
昨日市场上国产小麦出现新的改善，持有者保持售价稳定，因为本节经销商需求旺盛，许多中国面粉厂要求大量进货以充实库存。因此，价格较上次收盘价上涨0.05至0.10美元。大量新收国产小麦从内地产区运抵港口。

CHINA PRESS.

AUG 4 1939

Rice Market

Slight business in white rice was done
in yesterday's market, because of the
high rate. All operators in the session
were reluctant to buy, awaiting further
improvement. The market received 2,400
bags of fresh rice supplies from the inter-
ior, coming by truck and rail.
Owing to the maximum price set by
the authorities of the Shanghai Municipal
Council and French Concession, the rice
holders refused to supply their high quality
white rice for liquidation in the market.
A small amount of lowest-grade stocked
rice was offered in selling, and the price
was quoted at a maximum rate of $20
per picul, but no business was done
throughout the entire session.
The outside market, it was reported,
was firm yesterday, and a considerable
business was done by all the operators
and retail shops. The unofficial selling
price rose by $0.50 above the preceding
day's close, and the first-grade Changshu
white rice was noted at $24, or $4 above
the maximum price, while the glutinous
rice stood at $22.50.
The rate of provincial rice was irre-
gularly high for selling yesterday, because
the market received a small shipment from
the interior. The market continued to
keep the maximum price for liquidation,
so that no brisk business was recorded
in the day's purchases. The outside
market showed a satisfactory business,
and the selling rate moved up by $0.50
above the previous close.
The total sales in the day were estimated
at 3,000 bags of provincial rice. The
first-grade Nanking provincial rice was
quoted at $19, with Wuhu provincial rice
at $17 to $18.50, as well as the low-
grade provincial rice at $16.50 per picul.

1939年8月4日

大米市场

昨日白米交易清淡，原因是价格高企。本节所有经营者均不愿购买，等待进一步好转。市场收到来自内地的2,400袋新鲜大米供应，通过卡车和铁路运抵。
由于上海公共租界工部局和法租界当局设定了最高限价，大米持有者拒绝供应其优质白米在市场清算。仅有少量最低等级的库存大米上市出售，报价为最高每担20美元，但整个交易节未达成任何交易。
据报道，昨日场外市场坚挺，所有经营者和零售店均达成了可观的交易。非官方售价较前一日收盘价上涨0.50美元，一等常熟白米 noted at 24美元，即高于最高限价4美元，而糯米价格为22.50美元。
昨日外省米售价不规则地走高，因为市场收到来自内地的小批量货物。市场继续维持最高限价进行清算，因此当日采购记录中未见活跃交易。场外市场显示交易令人满意，售价较前一收盘价上涨0.50美元。
当日外省米总销量估计为3,000袋。一等南京外省米报价为19美元，芜湖外省米为17至18.50美元，低等级外省米为每担16.50美元。

Flour And Wheat

Because of keen demand by the outport
operators a satisfactory business in native
flour was seen in the market yesterday,
while the mills supplied a limited amount
of goods for liquidation for both local
buyers and outport merchants, because the
selling price remained at $4.85 in cash.
The Tientsin dealers took an active in-
terest in buying for transportation to
North China, and Southern traders bought
a considerable amount for shipments to
Canton and Amoy. Local buyers and
the interior deals absorbed 20,000 bags
of different kinds of the second-grade
product.
According to official reports in the
market, an increased selling price will be
asked of outport dealers in a day or two.
The new price will be from $0.05 to $0.10
per bag higher.
The selling rate of newly-harvested native
wheat showed firm in yesterday's market,
and a favorable business was recorded
throughout the session. The local buyers
took great interest in buying a big amount
of this wheat, but the mills were reluctant
to absorb for stocks. The total purchases
in the market amounted to 2,000 bags of
Nanking, Taiyung and Quansan newly-
harvested native wheat and the price re-
mained reasonable at $6.45 to $6.85 per
bag.

据市场官方报告，一两天后将要求外埠商人提高售价。新价格将每袋高出0.05至0.10美元。

CHINA PRESS

JUL 2 1936

Flour And Wheat

Since the drop of Chinese national currency in the past few days, the selling price of native flour has been kept nominal by all the mills. With large demands from outport dealers, the price of second-grade product native flour moved up by $0.10 per bag for both local and outport buyers.
Although a high discount on order cheque existed in the exchange market, there has been continued interest in North China and South Sea, but no big order of this flour was seen in the market, and fractional buying was recorded, because of shortage of cash. The selling rate of this wheat was heavily increased by the mills to outport dealers, and the rate quoted at $5.50 per bag, and paid in order cheque.
Local and the interior operators were willing to buy native flour, although the rate moved up $0.10 higher to $4.75. The total sales in the day amounted to 80,000 bags of different marks of second-grade native flour.
Trading in native wheat was narrow in yesterday's market, while the mills were not interested in buying. The Japanese mills were also reluctant to absorb yesterday. Both local dealers and South Sea merchants bought 1,700 bags of Soochow, Changshu and Quinsan native newly-harvested wheat at from $6.75 to $6.55 per bag.

面粉与小麦

鉴于近几日中国法币汇率下跌，各面粉厂对本地面粉的售价均维持名义价格。由于外埠客商需求旺盛，二等国产面粉对本地及外埠买家的价格每袋上涨0.10美元。
尽管汇票在汇市上存在高额贴现，华北及南洋地区仍持续保持兴趣，但因现金短缺，市场上未见该面粉的大宗订单，仅见零星购买记录。各面粉厂大幅提高了向外埠客商出售小麦的售价，报价为每袋5.50美元，以汇票支付。
尽管价格上涨0.10美元至4.75美元，本地及内地经营者仍愿意购买国产面粉。当日各类品牌的二等国产面粉总销量达80,000袋。

CHINA PRESS.

MAY 26 19□□

Flour And Wheat

Business conditions in the flour
market were very quiet and steady
yesterday. No brisk demand was
shown, but a favorable fractional
selling was reported.

Owing to the large stocks in go-
down, the North China operators
were not purchasing further cargoes
for transportation. South Sea buy-
ers took active interest, absorbing a
small amount.

Local and interior traders also
bought a few thousand bags at a
fair price. The total sales for the
day reached 30,000 bags.

The mills opened the second-
grade product in yesterday's session
at $6.40 cash and additional $0.20
paid by order check.

The opening price of native
wheat in yesterday's market was
steady and firm, with small turnover
reported for the day.

With small shipments of native
wheat brought here from the
interior, the holders refused to sell
their goods at a cheap price to
operators in the early morning's
session, and the market returned to
nominal shortly before the closing
of the morning's trading.

Various mills were not interested
in absorbing additional native
wheat, owing to an oversupply of
foreign wheat in stocks. Japanese
merchants bought a few hundred
bags of native wheat at $6.10.

19□□年5月26日

面粉与小麦

昨日面粉市场行情非常平静且稳定。未出现强劲需求，但据报道有有利的零星销售。

由于仓库库存量大，华北经营者未进一步采购货物用于运输。南洋买家表现出积极兴趣，吸纳了少量货物。

本地及内地贸易商也以合理价格购买了数千袋。当日总销量达到30,000袋。

各面粉厂在昨日交易中开出的二等产品价格为现金6.40美元，另加汇票支付0.20美元。

昨日市场国产小麦开盘价平稳坚挺，据报道当日成交量较小。

由于从内地运抵此处的国产小麦发货量较少，持货者在早市阶段拒绝以低价向经营者出售货物，市场在上午交易结束前不久恢复为名义价格。

由于库存中外麦供过于求，各家面粉厂对吸纳更多国产小麦不感兴趣。日本商人以6.10美元的价格购买了数百袋国产小麦。

Translation of a notice dated October 1, 1941 issued by
the Shanghai Municipality Rice Shop Owners' Association
on the subject of the distribution of rice imported by
the Shanghai Rice Granary Control Committee.

In a notification sent to this Association, the
Shanghai Rice Granary Control Committee states that the
Committee has resolved to request this Association to
distribute among the member shops some 50,000 bags of Rangoon
Rice at a price of $133.75 per bag of 224 lbs (including the
weight of the sack), computed at $107 per zar, to be
retailed to the public at maximum selling price of
$110 per zar of 160 catties net delivered weight, the
sale to commence at all rice shops in this locality at 9 a.m.
October 11.

As the cheap sale is for the benefit of those
people who live from hand to mouth, each person is
limited to the purchase of not more than one zar.

At a meeting of its Executive Committee, this
Association has decided to distribute the rice among its
member shops, prior to which this Association will undertake
a registration of the shops, the dates for which have been
specified as follows :-
Member shops in the International Settlement .........October 3
Member shops in the French Concession ...............October 4
Member shops in the Hongkew District................October 5
Member shops in the Western District ................October 6

The quantities to be allotted to the shops will
be 100 bags, 50 bags or 25 bags. No allotment will be
made to shops without retail facilities.

All the member shops are hereby notified to
detail their representatives to register with this
Association between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. on the dates
specified.

Shanghai Municipality Rice
Shop Owners' Association
October 1, 1941.

上海市米业同业公会于1941年10月1日发布的关于分配上海米粮管理委员会进口大米事宜的通知译文。

上海米粮管理委员会在向本会发出的通知中表示，委员会已决定请求本会将约50,000袋仰光米分配给会员店铺，价格为每袋224磅（含麻袋重量）133.75美元，按每担107美元计算，零售给公众的最高售价为每担160斤净重交货价110美元，销售将于10月11日上午9时在本地所有米店开始。

由于此次廉价销售旨在惠及那些生计艰难的人群，每人限购不超过一担。

在本会执行委员会会议上，本会决定将此批大米分配给会员店铺，在此之前，本会将进行店铺登记，具体日期规定如下：
公共租界内的会员店铺 .........10月3日
法租界内的会员店铺 ...............10月4日
虹口区的会员店铺................10月5日
西区会员店铺 ................10月6日

分配给各店铺的数量将为100袋、50袋或25袋。不具备零售条件的店铺不予分配。

特此通知所有会员店铺，在上述指定日期的上午9时至下午5时之间，派遣代表到本会进行登记。

上海市米业同业公会
1941年10月1日。

Sol, Special Branch..........Station. File No.................... Date August 23, 1941

SUBJECT: The Shanghai Rice Granary Control Committee-
cheap sale of rice.

The Shanghai Rice Granary Control Committee,
which was sponsored about the end of 1940 by Mr. T.K.
Ho, Deputy Secretary of the S.M.C., Mr. Yu Ya Ching
and some leading members of the rice trade with the
object to import rice to improve the rice situation,
commenced its first cheap sale of rice on August 23
through twenty six rice shops in the International
Settlement and twenty shops in the French Concession.
The rice for sale consists of 3,734 bags of 2nd grade
Siam rice, and it is being sold at $116.00 per "zar"
of 80 kilograms and each person is limited to the
purchase of not more than one "zar." The market
price of commercial rice of this grade ranges from
$120.00 to $124.00 per "zar."

It is learned that this stock of 3,734 bags
was purchased locally by the Committee sometime ago.
The Committee is ordering 50,000 bags of Rangoon rice
for further cheap sales, and this consignment is
expected to arrive here sometime in September.

A list of the rice shops entrusted with the sale
of the rice of the Committee, with quantities alloted
to each shop, has been received from the Committee and
is attached hereto with translation. The list was
also published in the local press today.

（印：FILE）

（批：glc 23.8.41）

主题：上海米粮管理委员会——大米廉价销售。

上海米粮管理委员会由工部局副秘书长何德奎 (T.K. Ho) 先生、虞洽卿 (Yu Ya Ching) 先生及部分米业领袖于1940年底发起成立，旨在通过进口大米改善米粮状况，该委员会于8月23日通过公共租界的26家米店和法租界的20家米店开始了首次大米廉价销售。待售大米包括3,734袋二等暹罗米，售价为每“担”（80公斤）116.00美元，每人限购不超过一“担”。该等级商业大米的市场价格在每“担”120.00美元至124.00美元之间。

据悉，这3,734袋库存是委员会前一段时间在本地购买的。委员会正在订购50,000袋仰光米以进行进一步的廉价销售，预计这批货物将于9月的某个时候抵达此处。

委员会已发来一份受委托销售其大米的米店名单及各店分配数量，附后并附译文。该名单也于今日在当地报刊上刊登。

POLICE FORCE
28 MAR 1941

Translation of letter to Chinese Deputy
Secretary from the Shanghai Rice Cheap
Sale Committee.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
Dated 25th March, 1941. S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8298/5W-5
Address: No.93 Canton Road. Date / 4 H
Tel. 16674.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 25 MAR. 1941）

Rice: Cheap sales to be discontinued.

This committee has already conducted cheap sales of rice
for eight periods. It was our intention to continue work for
another period before winding up. However, our stock of rice
is no longer adequate and it is difficult to secure further
contributions. Moreover, the various rice shops entrusted with
the work have one after another complained to us on account of
the difficulties they have met with, and have refused to
continue sales. The problem of how to improve the method of
maintaining order during the sales is also not easily solved.
Because of these reasons we have decided to discontinue the
work forthwith and to transfer our rice stock to various
philanthropic organizations to be used for the sale of cooked
rice at cheap price and for free distribution of congee. These
undertakings will be carried out under our own supervision.
The Council has addressed a letter to us intimating that it
does not object to the above-mentioned arrangement. At our
89th ordinary meeting a resolution to take the above stated
step has also been passed. Kindly take note.
(Signed) Tu Ho-ch'ing, Chairman.

(Note: Received for translation 1st Apr. 28th March, 1941.)

Alliance
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL TRANSLATION OFFICE MAR 28 1941）

上海大米廉价销售委员会致华人副总办的信函译文。
上海公共租界工部局警务处
日期 1941年3月25日。 特别处登记室
编号 S. B. D. 8298/5W-5
地址：广东路93号。 日期 / 4 H
电话 16674。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处处长办公室 1941年3月25日）

大米：停止廉价销售。

本委员会已进行了八期大米廉价销售。我们原计划在结束工作前再进行一期。然而，我们的米粮库存已不再充足，且难以获得更多的捐助。此外，受委托开展此项工作的各家米店因遇到的困难相继向我们投诉，并拒绝继续销售。如何改进销售期间维持秩序的方法也是一个不易解决的问题。鉴于这些原因，我们决定立即停止此项工作，并将我们的米粮库存移交给各慈善组织，用于廉价销售熟饭和免费分发粥品。这些活动将在我们自己的监督下进行。工部局已致函我方，表示不反对上述安排。在我方第89次常会上，也已通过采取上述步骤的决议。请知悉。
（签名） 杜浩清 (Tu Ho-ch'ing)，主席。

（注：收到翻译件 1941年3月28日 4月1日。）

Alliance
（印章：上海公共租界工部局翻译处 1941年3月28日）

It is noted from your letter that in response to
the Council's request that the cheap sales of rice should
be conducted in a more satisfactory manner your Committee
has made arrangements for hot congee and cheap cooked rice
to be distributed from the centres mentioned in your letter.
The Council has no objection to this procedure which it is
understood will be less troublesome and lead to less abuse
than the former practice of selling uncooked rice.

I have again to express the Council's appreciation
of the charitable work undertaken by your Committee on
behalf of the needy of Shanghai and to enclose herewith
the Council's cheque for $10,000 being its second contri-
bution towards this cause.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient Servant,

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL SECRETARY'S OFFICE 1 MAR. 1941）

T. K. HO
Deputy Secretary.

Members of Council.

Cheap Sales of Rice.

There is attached copy of a report by the Commissioner of Police, with departmental reports, regarding the unsatisfactory operation of the cheap sales of rice in the Settlement. Copy of a letter from the Shanghai Rice Shops' Association is also attached.

In November, last, the Council decided to make a grant towards the funds contributed to finance the cheap sales of rice of a sum of $10,000 per month for a period of three months, the matter to be reviewed thereafter. The French Municipal Administration agreed to make a grant of half the amount contributed by the Council for the same purpose. So far the sum of ¥10,000 has been paid by the Council and the question now arises as to whether in the circumstances the Council feels that any further payment should be made. In its letter to the Cheap Sales Committee promising a grant of $30,000 the Council attached no qualifications to the grant.

POLICE FORCE
January 24, 1941.

Secretary & Commissioner General,
S. M. C.

Reference. Your File No. F.30/12
Letter from Shanghai Rice Shops'
Association dated January 15, 1941
Subject : Cheap Rice Sales.

I forward herewith copy of a Police report on the subject.
These sales are most unsatisfactory from a Police point
of view for the following reasons:-
(1) The unruly crowds which necessitate the posting of a large
number of police who could be better employed.
(2) The majority of the purchasers are Non-Residents of the
Settlement.
(3) The "racket" of employing a lot of children to buy for the
purpose of resale.
(4) The opportunities and allegations against the Police regarding
the purchase of tickets.
(5) The allegation against shop assistants retaining large numbers
of tickets for themselves.
(6) The allegation that the shops selling the rice unload some of
their inferior stock (no corroborative proof of this).
(7) The loss of business to the shops selling tickets and all the
other shops in the vicinity.
(8) As in the case of other cheap sales such as flour and bread,
the police wish it to be carried out as quietly and unobtru-
sively as possible. The sponsors on the other hand like the
publicity and "face" of seeing large crowds being photographed
by newspapermen.

Instructions will be issued that Police officers
must not purchase cheap rice tickets.

K.M. Bourne,
Commissioner of Police.

事由：贵方档案编号 F.30/12
1941年1月15日上海米业公会来信
主题：平价米销售。

现随函转去一份关于此事的警务报告副本。
从警务角度来看，这些销售活动极为令人不满，原因如下：
(1) 人群秩序混乱，需要部署大量警力，而这些警力本可用于其他更合适的用途。
(2) 大多数购买者并非租界居民。
(3) 雇佣大量儿童代购以便转售的“勾当”。
(4) 有关购买票券方面针对警方的机会主义行为及指控。
(5) 有关店员为自己保留大量票券的指控。
(6) 有关出售大米的商店借机处理部分劣质库存的指控（此项无确凿证据佐证）。
(7) 导致售票商店及周边所有其他商店生意受损。
(8) 正如面粉和面包等其他平价销售的情况一样，警方希望销售过程尽可能安静且不引人注目。另一方面，发起方则喜欢这种宣传效应，以及看到记者拍摄大规模人群所带来的“面子”。

将发出指令，规定警务人员不得购买平价米票券。

K.M. Bourne,
警务处处长。

January 22, 1941.

Commissioner,
D. C. (Divisions).

Allegations against members of the
Police re sale of cheap rice.

Resultant enquiries (attached report) substantiate
the allegations that members of the Police Force (Chinese
Branch) have been purchasing large numbers of cheap rice
coupons for their own personal use during the progress of
the cheap rice sale.

No intimidation was actually used in obtaining the
coupons which were apparently sold by the respective shops
staff as a friendly gesture in order to keep on good terms
with the Police on duty in the respective districts.

Under the circumstances that employees of these
shops refuse to give the numbers of any of the policemen
purchasing these coupons, the large number of police
who have been involved in the purchasing of these coupons,
no disciplinary action can be taken against any individual.

The sale of cheap rice was discontinued on 20-1-41.

This complaint from the Shanghai Rice Shops Associa-
tion corroborates the police report of 17-1-41 re the
difficulty of the control of the crowds outside these shops
engaged in the sale of cheap rice and is an additional
argument why the sales should be discontinued pending
arrangements being made for a more satisfactory method
of distribution.

1941年1月22日。

致：
分区警务总监。

关于警务人员涉及平价米销售的指控。

随后的调查（附报告）证实了以下指控：在平价米销售期间，警务处成员（华捕部门）购买了大量平价米票券供个人使用。

在获取这些票券的过程中，实际上并未使用任何胁迫手段；这些票券显然是由各店店员作为友好姿态出售的，目的是与在各辖区执勤的警察保持良好关系。

鉴于这些商店的雇员拒绝透露任何购买这些票券的警察的姓名，且卷入购买此类票券的警察人数众多，因此无法对任何个人采取纪律处分。

平价米销售已于1941年1月20日停止。

上海米业公会的这封投诉信佐证了1941年1月17日关于控制从事平价米销售的商店外人群困难的警务报告，并为应在安排更令人满意的分配方法之前停止销售提供了额外的理由。

Cheap Rice Sales.

With reference to the attached letter from the

No.1 Ticket Selling Shop - Heng Shing Loong
(                 ), 14 North Che...ng Road

On 10.1.41 p.m., after the daily allotment of

No.3 Ticket Selling Shop - Heng Foong Chong

page_data.en:
3.

A complaint by the shop management to the Shanghai
Rice Shop Owners' Association resulted in the Association
advising the shop, by telephone, to sell not more than 5 tickets
to each C.P.C.

In no case was there any evidence or complaint of the
shops staff having been intimidated into selling tickets to
C.P.C.s and apparently the tickets were sold to them merely as
a friendly gesture on the part of the shop keepers, who are
anxious to keep on friendly terms with a uniform policeman who
is doing duty in the district.

All the employees of the shops in question were either
unable or unwilling to divulge the numbers or names of any of
the C.P.C.s who purchased the cheap rice tickets but it is fairly
obvious that they could give such information if they so desired.

Another scheme allegedly used by C.P.C.s to obtain
tickets was to approach the sellers and ask for tickets for
supposed aged and feeble women who were at the end of line
awaiting their turn.

It should also be noted that under the existing condi-
tions for the sale of these tickets; there appears to be nothing
to prevent unscrupulous shop assistants, employed in the Ticket
Selling Shops, from retaining and selling large batches of the
tickets to their own personal friends, if they wished to do so.

The conclusion arrived at is, that most of the shops
assigned to sell the tickets were reluctant to continue the
sales owing to excessive demands for tickets made by C.P.C.s
and the inconvenience and loss of business, besides minor
damage caused to other shop keepers in the vicinity.
page_data.zh:
3.

店方管理层向上海米业公会投诉，导致公会通过电话建议该店，向每名华捕（C.P.C.）出售的票证不得超过 5 张。

在任何情况下，均无证据或投诉表明店员受到胁迫而向华捕出售票证；显然，店主出售票证给他们仅仅是出于友好姿态，因为他们渴望与在该辖区执勤的制服警察保持友好关系。

涉事店铺的所有雇员要么无法、要么不愿透露任何购买廉价米票的华捕的编号或姓名，但很明显，如果他们愿意，是可以提供这些信息的。

据称，华捕获取票证的另一种手段是接近售票员，要求为那些在队伍末尾等候、 purportedly（声称是）年老体弱的妇女购买票证。

还应注意，在这些票证销售的现有条件下，似乎没有任何措施能防止售票店中不诚实的店员如果愿意的话，截留并将大批票证出售给他们自己的私人朋友。

得出的结论是，大多数被指派销售票证的店铺因华捕对票证的过度需求、造成的不便和生意损失，以及对附近其他店主造成的轻微损害，而不愿继续销售。

page_data.en:
F 30/12.

Translation of letter to Chinese Deputy
Secretary from the Shanghai Rice Shops'
Association.

Dated 15th January, 1941.

Address. No.52, Lane 153,
Shanhaikwan Road.

Rice. Cheap sales stopped.

The eighth period for the cheap sale of rice began on the
7th instant and ends on the15th. Many shops entrusted with the
sale, faced difficulties in the work and found it impossible to
continue; they have written to us to request permission to
suspend sales. Six establishments in the International
Settlement have definitely refused to co-operate; these have
already stopped selling. On enquiry we find that the reasons
for their refusal are as follows:-

1. During this period each person is allowed to purchase two
dollars' worth of rice at a time. Fifty bags of rice are only
sufficient to meet the requirements of from 1200 to 1300 persons.
When the tickets are sold out the shops are suspected of holding
back the rice. The poor who bear a grudge against the
establishments, often use abusive language, clamour loudly and
throw bricks and filth at the premises. In consequence disorder
prevails.

2. In the early morning several thousand poor people gather
daily in front of each shop. In the afternoon, as time approaches
the
for the sale of tickets and the Police arrive on/scene, disorder
begins and the crowd becomes difficult to control. Not a single
day has passed without some window, door or counter of a shop, or
the glass of the show-window of a neighbouring establishment,
being damaged.

3. Police Constables frequently purchase large numbers of tickets
from the shops, thereby reducing the chance of the poor to obtain
rice. More than a thousand disappointed persons are often found
daily outside each shop. They create much disturbance, but no one
takes any step to disperse them.

F 30/12.

上海米业公会致华人副秘书长的信函译文。

日期：1941年1月15日。

地址：山海关路153弄52号。

大米。停止廉价销售。

第八期大米廉价销售于本月7日开始，至15日结束。许多受托销售的店铺在工作中面临困难，发现无法继续；他们已致函我们，请求允许暂停销售。公共租界内有六家商号明确拒绝合作；这些商号已经停止销售。经查询，我们发现其拒绝的原因如下：-

1. 在此期间，每人每次允许购买价值两元的大米。五十袋大米仅够满足1200至1300人的需求。当票证售罄时，店铺被怀疑囤积大米。对商号怀恨在心的贫民经常使用辱骂性语言，大声喧哗，并向店铺投掷砖块和污物。结果导致秩序混乱。

2. 每天清晨，数千名贫民聚集在每家店铺门前。下午，随着售票时间临近且警察到达现场，混乱开始，人群变得难以控制。没有一天不发生店铺的窗户、门或柜台，或邻近商号橱窗玻璃受损的情况。

3. 巡捕经常从店铺购买大量票证，从而减少了贫民获得大米的机会。每天每家店铺外往往有一千多名失望的人。他们制造了许多骚乱，但无人采取任何措施驱散他们。

page_data.en:
4. After Constables A and B have purchased whole batches of tickets
from a shop (in some cases, shops are instructed by Police Officers
to reserve tickets for them), Constables C and D arrive and desire
to obtain tickets for themselves. The tickets being sold out, the
disappointed Police officers, after ascertaining that only about a
thousand poor people have obtained their shares of the 50 bags daily
allotment, accuse the shop of withholding rice for profit. They
demand to see the counterfoils, find fault with the shop and often
refuse to be appeased even after the reason for the shortage in the
number of tickets has been fully explained to them.
For instance, an employe of the No.7 ticket selling shop, Tung
Meu ( ), in Wuting Road was taken to a police station on the
13th, and an employe of the No.9 ticket selling shop, Pao T'a ( )
in Ferry Road was taken on the 14th, both for the same reasons.
Although they were later released, the shops have suffered consider-
able annoyance.
5. The breaking of bags to steal the rice transported daily to
shops for cheap sale is becoming more frequent. Shops fear to carry
on the sales because of the heavy losses involved.
The above are the true reasons for the suspension of the sales
by the various shops which are unable to cope with the situation.
A few days ago the iron grille and counters of the Nos.1, 3, 8 and
10 ticket selling shops were damaged; the glass windows fell down
and nearly caused a serious mishap.
Yesterday the sale of cheap rice at Ta Fung Nyi (No.12 Sales
Dept), Connaught Road, could not be effected in an orderly manner
because Chinese policeman purchased rice tickets in large numbers;
even foreign Constables failed to restore order. Several hundreds
of poor people waited in front of the shop till as late as seven
o'clock in the evening. When foreign Constables returned, the shop
began to sell, and could not close until after the departure of the
poor people. Owing to these difficulties we cannot compel the
various rice shops to continue the cheap sales. This report shows
clearly the difficulties that the rice shops are confronted with.
(Chopped) Rice Shops' Association.
page_data.zh:
4. 在巡捕 A 和 B 从一家店铺购买整批票证后（在某些情况下，店铺接到警官指令为他们预留票证），巡捕 C 和 D 到达并希望为自己获取票证。由于票证已售罄，失望的警官在得知每日配给的50袋大米中仅有约一千名贫民获得了份额后，指责店铺为牟利而囤积大米。他们要求查看存根，对店铺吹毛求疵，即使在向他们充分解释了票证数量短缺的原因后，往往仍不肯罢休。
例如，吴淞路第7号售票店“同美”（Tung Meu，音译）的一名雇员于13日被带往警察局，渡轮路（Ferry Road）第9号售票店“宝泰”（Pao T'a，音译）的一名雇员于14日被带走，原因相同。虽然他们后来获释，但店铺遭受了相当大的困扰。
5. 拆破米袋以盗窃每日运往店铺进行廉价销售的大米的情况日益频繁。店铺因涉及重大损失而害怕继续销售。
以上是各店铺因无法应对局势而暂停销售的真实原因。
前几天，第1、3、8和10号售票店的铁栅栏和柜台受损；玻璃窗坠落，险些造成严重事故。
昨天，康纳路（Connaught Road）大丰怡（Ta Fung Nyi，第12销售部）的廉价大米销售无法有序进行，因为中国警察大量购买米票；甚至外籍巡捕也未能恢复秩序。数百名贫民在店前等待直至晚上七点钟。当外籍巡捕返回时，店铺开始销售，直到贫民离开后才得以关门。由于这些困难，我们无法强迫各家米店继续廉价销售。本报告清楚地显示了米店所面临的困难。
（盖章）米业公会。

F 30/12
Translation of letter to Deputy
Secretary T. K. Ho from Shanghai
Rice Cheap Sales Committee.
Dated 17th February, 1941.
Tel.16674. Address: 33 Canton Road.

Rice! Arrangements for Cheap sales.

We have received your letter enclosing a Police report
on cheap sales of rice. The report was brought up for discussion
at the 19th meeting of our Standing Committee, and a translation
was read by all the members present.

With regard to the cheap sales conducted by this Associa-
tion the report contains the following views:
(1) The people benefitted by the cheap sales are not residents
in the Settlement and the French Concession. This is con-
trary to the Council's order prohibiting the transportation
of rice out of the Settlement.
(2) The number of Police for the maintenance of order should be
increased.
(3) If no suitable arrangement can be made to limit the sales
to the residents in the Settlement, the cheap sales should
be suspended.
(4) The officials of the Salvation Army are confident that they
can find a way to deal with the matter.

This Committee has conducted cheap sale of rice already
for eight periods. We have time and again discussed the problem of
improving the sale procedure, but so far no satisfactory method
has been found. Regarding the point that purchasers of rice are
not Settlement or French Concession residents, it is stated in
the report that the Police themselves have been unable to distinguish
between residents and non-residents, or to prevent a suspected
non-resident from making purchase. In view of this statement we
wonder by what method the Police have been able to arrive at the
percentage of non-resident purchasers as referred to in the report.
page_data.zh:
F 30/12
上海米业平价销售委员会致副秘书长何德奎（T. K. Ho）的信函译文。
日期：1941年2月17日。
电话：16674。地址：广东路33号。

大米！廉价销售安排。

我们已收到你附寄的关于大米廉价销售的警务报告。该报告已在我会常务委员会第十九次会议上提出讨论，并由所有出席成员宣读了译文。

关于本会进行的廉价销售，报告包含以下观点：
(1) 受益于廉价销售的人士并非租界及法租界的居民。这违背了工部局禁止将大米运出租界的命令。
(2) 应增加维持秩序的警察人数。
(3) 如果无法做出适当安排将销售限制在租界居民范围内，则应暂停廉价销售。
(4) 救世军官员确信他们能找到处理此事的方法。

本委员会已进行了八期大米廉价销售。我们曾多次讨论改进销售程序的问题，但至今未找到令人满意的方法。关于购米者非租界或法租界居民这一点，报告中指出警察本身无法区分居民与非居民，也无法阻止疑似非居民进行购买。鉴于这一陈述，我们想知道警察是通过何种方法得出报告中提到的非居民购买者比例的。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

The object of this Committee is to afford relief to the poor. In
the past year we have solicited and obtained contributions
totalling more than a million dollars from various organizations
and individuals. So long as the purchasers are Chinese, no dis-
crimination should be made. Moreover, as a matter of fact, it is
impossible to identify the purchasers.

We are very grateful to the Police for the additional
work performed by them in maintaining peace and order during the
sales.

As for the 8th period we have received many reports from
rice shops stating that disturbances were created by some bad
characters who insisted on making large purchases and were angry
with the shops. We presume that the details have already been
reported to the police. Because a few rice shops were unwilling
to continue the sales, the work for the 8th period was suspended.
Besides, the Rice Shops Association has written to state that all
rice shops would hereafter refuse to undertake the work, and we
do not know how to cope with the situation. While this matter is
now being carefully considered, we are distributing congee and
cheap rice in the premises of the Nich Wong Sei Branch Temple
Wuting Road, in the name of Nyi Chi Benevolent Association, and in
the premises of the Native Banks' Association, North Honan Road,
in the name of the Yellow Swastika Society. All broken rice is
supplied by this Committee at reduced price so that the poor and
needy may be directly benefitted. As the staff of the Salvation
Army are confident that they are able to devise efficient measures
to conduct cheap sale, and also they are trusted by the Police
Authorities, the Council may permit them to undertake this work.
As soon as we are notified of their definite plan, the ten thousand
dollars now in our possession and the remaining part of the
$30,000 and $15,000, donations from the Shanghai Municipal Council
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

本委员会的宗旨是为贫民提供救济。在过去一年中，我们从各组织和个人那里募集并获得了超过一百万元的捐款。只要购买者是中国人，就不应有所歧视。此外，事实上，要识别购买者是不可能的。

我们对警察在销售期间为维护和平与秩序所做的额外工作表示非常感谢。

至于第八期，我们收到许多米店的报告，称一些不良分子坚持大量购买并对店铺发怒，制造了骚乱。我们推测细节已向警方报告。由于几家米店不愿继续销售，第八期的工作被迫暂停。此外，米业公会来函声明，今后所有米店将拒绝承担此项工作，我们不知如何应对此局面。在此事正在仔细考虑之际，我们以“仁济善堂”（Nyi Chi Benevolent Association，音译）的名义在吴淞路泥城寺支庙（Nich Wong Sei Branch Temple，音译）内，并以“黄卍字会”（Yellow Swastika Society）的名义在河南路钱业公会内，分发粥和廉价大米。所有碎米均由本委员会以低价供应，以便贫苦民众直接受益。由于救世军工作人员确信他们能够制定有效措施来进行廉价销售，并且他们受到警察当局的信任，工部局可以允许他们承担这项工作。一旦我们获悉他们的具体计划，目前由我们掌握的的一万元，以及来自上海公共租界工部局

page_data.en:
- 5 -
and the French Council respectively, may be handed to the said
Army. These are the resolutions of our committee meeting.
Please note.

(Signed) Yu Ya-ching,

Chairman.
page_data.zh:
- 5 -
和法国公董局分别捐赠的三万元和一万元捐款的剩余部分，可移交给上述救世军。这是我们委员会会议的决议。
请知悉。

（签名）虞洽卿，

主席。

quietly and unobtrusively as possible. The system

January 23, 1941.

Commissioner of Police.

The attached report is a further argument
against these cheap rice sales. The main points are :-
(1) The unruly crowds which necessitate the posting of
a large number of police who could be better employed.
(2) The majority of the purchasers come from O.C.L.
(3) The racket of employing a lot of children to buy
for the purpose of resale.
(4) The opportunity and allegations against the Police
regarding the purchase of tickets.
(5) The allegation against shop assistants retaining large
numbers of tickets for themselves.
(6) The allegation that the shops selling the rice
unload some of their inferior stock (no corroborative
proof of this ).
(7) The loss of business to the shops selling tickets
and all the other shops in the vicinity.
(8) As in the case of other cheap sales such as flour
and bread, the police wish it to be carried out
as quietly and unobtrusively as possible. The sponsors
on the other hand like the publicity and "face"
of seeing large crowds being photographed by
newspapermen.

It is very difficult to suggest any solution.
It is too big for the Salvation Army to handle and I doubt
if the Rice Guilds would take over the distribution
themselves.

D.C. (Divisions)
page_data.zh:
1941年1月23日。

警务总监。

随附报告进一步提出了反对这些廉价大米销售的理由。主要论点如下：-
(1) 需要部署大量警力来维持秩序的不守规矩的人群，而这些警力本可用于更合适的地方。
(2) 大多数购买者来自越界筑路区（O.C.L.）。
(3) 雇佣许多儿童代为购买以便转售的投机行为。
(4) 关于购票过程中针对警方的机会主义行为和指控。
(5) 关于店员为自己保留大量票证的指控。
(6) 关于出售大米的商店借机清理部分劣质库存的指控（对此无确凿证据）。
(7) 售票商店及附近所有其他商店的业务损失。
(8) 正如面粉和面包等其他廉价销售的情况一样，警方希望尽可能安静和不引人注目地进行。而另一方面，发起方则喜欢这种 publicity（宣传）和“面子”，即看到大批人群被报馆摄影师拍照。

很难提出任何解决方案。
这对救世军来说规模太大，难以处理，我也怀疑米业公会是否愿意亲自接管分发工作。

分区副总监 (Divisions)

January 22, 1941.

Commissioner. (2)
D. C. (Divisions). ✓

Allegations against members of the
Police re sale of cheap rice.

Resultant enquiries (attached report) substantiate
the allegations that members of the Police Force (Chinese
Branch) have been purchasing large numbers of cheap rice
coupons for their own personal use during the progress of
the cheap rice sale.

No intimidation was actually used in obtaining the
coupons which were apparently sold by the respective shops
staff as a friendly gesture in order to keep on good terms
with the Police on duty in the respective districts.

Under the circumstances that employees of these
shops refuse to give the numbers of any of the policemen
purchasing these coupons, the large number of police
who have been involved in the purchasing of these coupons,
no disciplinary action can be taken against any individual.

The sale of cheap rice was discontinued on 20-1-41.

This complaint from the Shanghai Rice Shops Associa-
tion corroborates the police report of 17-1-41 re the
difficulty of the control of the crowds outside these shops
engaged in the sale of cheap rice and is an additional

关于警方成员涉及廉价大米销售的指控。

随后的调查（见附报告）证实了以下指控：在廉价大米销售期间，警察部队（华捕股）的成员一直在购买大量廉价大米票证供个人使用。

在获取这些票证时并未实际使用恐吓手段，这些票证显然是由各店职员作为友好姿态出售的，目的是为了与各自辖区执勤的警方保持良好关系。

鉴于这些商店的雇员拒绝提供任何购买这些票证的警员编号，且卷入购买这些票证的警员人数众多，因此无法对任何个人采取纪律行动。

廉价大米销售已于1941年1月20日停止。

上海米店业同业的这一投诉佐证了1941年1月17日关于控制从事廉价大米销售的商店外人群困难的警方报告，并提供了额外的理由，说明为何在安排更令人满意的分配方法之前，应停止销售。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特务科 1941年1月22日）

friends, if they wished to do so.

shops assigned to sell the tickets were reluctant to continue
the sales owing to excessive demands for tickets made by

相关商店的所有雇员要么无法要么不愿透露任何购买廉价大米票证的华捕的编号或姓名，但很明显，如果他们愿意，是可以提供这些信息的。
据称华捕获取票证使用的另一种方案是接近卖家，索要票证，声称是给排在队尾等候轮候的年迈体弱妇女购买的。
还应注意，在这些票证销售的现有条件下，似乎没有什么能防止售票商店中不择手段的店员如果愿意的话，保留并向自己的私人朋友大批出售票证。

Dated 15th January, 1941.
Address: No. 52, Lane 153,
Shanhaikwan Road.

(批：urgent steps are necessary)
(印：JAN 16 1941)

Rice: Cheap sales stopped.

The eighth period for the cheap sale of rice began on the
7th instant and ends on the 15th. Many shops entrusted with the
sale, faced difficulties in the work and found it impossible to
continue; they have written to us to request permission to
suspend sales. Six establishments in the International
Settlement have definitely refused to co-operate; these have
already stopped selling. On enquiry we find that the reasons
for their refusal are as follows:-

1. During this period each person is allowed to purchase two
dollars' worth of rice at a time. Fifty bags of rice are only
sufficient to meet the requirements of from 1200 to 1300 persons.
When the tickets are sold out the shops are suspected of holding
back the rice. The poor who bear a grudge against the
establishments, often use abusive language, clamour loudly and
throw bricks and filth at the premises. In consequence disorder
prevails.

2. In the early morning several thousand poor people gather
daily in front of each shop. In the afternoon, as time
approaches for the sale of tickets and the Police arrive on
the scene, disorder begins and the crowd becomes difficult to
control. Not a single day has passed without some window,
door or counter of a shop, or the glass of the show-window
of a neighbouring establishment, being damaged.

(批：Serious)

日期：1941年1月15日。

(批注：需采取紧急措施)
(印章：1941年1月16日)

大米：平价销售已停止。

第八期大米平价销售始于本月7日，将于15日结束。许多受托销售的店铺在工作中面临困难，发现无法继续经营；它们已致函本会，请求准许暂停销售。公共租界内有六家商号明确拒绝合作；这些商号已经停止销售。经查询，我们发现其拒绝的原因如下：-

1. 在此期间，每人每次限购价值两元的大米。五十袋大米仅够满足1200至1300人的需求。当票券售罄时，店铺被怀疑囤积大米。对店铺怀恨在心的贫民，经常使用辱骂性语言，大声喧哗，并向店铺投掷砖块和污物。结果导致秩序混乱。

2. 每天清晨，数千名贫民聚集在每家店铺门前。下午，随着发售票券时间的临近以及警察到达现场，骚乱开始，人群变得难以控制。没有一天不发生店铺窗户、门或柜台，或邻近商号橱窗玻璃受损的情况。

(批注：严重)

page_data.en:
！
- 2 -

（批：These two have a complaint of this kind.）

3. Police Constables frequently purchase large numbers of tickets from the shops, thereby reducing the chance of the poor to obtain rice. More than a thousand disappointed persons are often found daily outside each shop. They create much disturbance, but no one takes any step to disperse them.
4. After Constables A and B have purchased whole batches of tickets from a shop (in some cases, shops are instructed by Police Officers to reserve tickets for them), Constables C and D arrive and desire to obtain tickets for themselves. The tickets being sold out, the disappointed Police officers, after ascertaining that only about a thousand poor people have obtained their shares of the 50 bags daily allotment, accuse the shop of withholding rice for profit. They demand to see the counter-foils, find fault with the shop and often refuse to be appeased even after the reason for the shortage in the number of tickets has been fully explained to them.
※ For instance, an employé of the No.7 ticket selling shop, Tung Meu (茂同), in Wuting Road was taken to a police station on the 13th, and an employé of the No.9 ticket selling shop, Pao T'a (太寶), in Ferry Road was taken on the 14th, both for the same reasons. Although they were later released, the shops have suffered considerable annoyance.
5. The breaking of bags to steal the rice transported daily to shops for cheap sale is becoming more frequent. Shops fear to carry on the sales because of the heavy losses involved.
The above are the true reasons for the suspension of the sales by the various shops which are unable to cope with the situation. A few days ago the iron grilles and counters of the Nos.1, 3, 8 and 10 ticket selling shops were damaged; the glass windows fell down and nearly caused a serious mishap.
※ Yesterday the sale of cheap rice at Ta Fung Nyi (No.12 Sales Depot), Connaught Road, could not be effected in an orderly manner because Chinese policemen purchased rice tickets in large numbers; even foreign Constables failed to restore order. Several hundreds of poor people waited in front of the

！
- 2 -

（批注：这两家有此类投诉。）

3. 巡捕经常从店铺购买大量票券，从而减少了贫民获得大米的机会。每天每家店铺外常有一千多名失望的人。他们制造了许多骚乱，但无人采取任何措施驱散他们。
4. 在巡捕A和B从一家店铺购买整批票券后（在某些情况下，店铺受警官指示为他们预留票券），巡捕C和D到达并希望为自己获取票券。由于票券已售罄，失望的警官在得知每日配给的50袋大米中仅有约一千名贫民获得了份额后，指责该店铺为牟利而扣留大米。他们要求查看票根存根，对店铺吹毛求疵，即使在向他们充分解释了票券数量短缺的原因后，往往仍不肯罢休。
※ 例如，吴淞路第7号售票处茂同（音译）的一名雇员于13日被带往警察局，斐伦路（今九江路）第9号售票处太寶（音译）的一名雇员于14日被带走，原因相同。虽然他们后来获释，但店铺遭受了相当大的困扰。
5. 拆破袋子偷窃每日运往店铺进行平价销售的大米的现象日益频繁。店铺因涉及重大损失而不敢继续销售。
以上是各店铺因无法应对局势而暂停销售的真实原因。日前，第1、3、8和10号售票处的铁栅栏和柜台遭到损坏；玻璃窗坠落，险些造成严重事故。
※ 昨天，康纳脱路（今海宁路）大丰義（第12号销售点）的平价大米销售因中国警察大量购买米票而无法有序进行；甚至外籍巡捕也未能恢复秩序。数百名贫民在店前等待，

shop till as late as seven o'clock in the evening. When foreign
Constables returned, the shop began to sell, and would not close
until after the departure of the poor people. Owing to these
difficulties we cannot compel the various rice shops to
continue the cheap sales. This report shows clearly the
difficulties that the rice shops are confronted with.
(Chopped) Rice Shops' Association.

January 16,1941.

D.C.(Divisions)
Commissioner.

Cheap Rice Sales.

The sale of cheap rice, sponsored by Mr. Yu Ya Ching
during September,1939, in which cheap rice and coupons to
obtain rice have been sold at 60 shops in the International
and French Concession is not proving to be of great material
assistance to the poorer class residents of the International
and French concession.

From statistics compiled by the officers in charge
of A and B Divisions in the International Settlement,
it is obvious that the very large proportion of people who
have bought this cheap rice since the eighth (8) sale which
commenced on 7-1-41 are not residents of the International
Settlement.

"A" Division records 16.9% residents of Settlement.
"B" Division records 40% residents of Settlement.
"C" Division records a very small percentage being residents
of the Settlement.

The French Police also report that the majority
of buyers of this rice in the French Concession are non-
residents.

Since the commencement of the last cheap rice sale
on 7-1-41 until 15-1-41 (inclusive) 421,000 people have taken
advantage of this sale, the majority of which as already
stated are non-residents of the International or French
Concession, a total of 1,500 bags of rice daily being sold,
the larger proportion of which is leaving the Settlement
despite Municipal Notification No. 4976 of 7-7-38 which
required permission from S.M. Police to remove rice from the
confines of the Settlement, which order was issued in order
to conserve the stocks of rice in the Settlement.

（批：S&C G. "Sp Per export"）
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 17 JAN. 1941 3）
page_data.zh:
1941年1月16日。

分区副总监
总监。

大米平价销售。

由虞洽卿先生于1939年9月发起的大米平价销售，在公共租界和法租界的60家店铺销售平价大米及购米券，事实证明这对公共租界和法租界的贫困居民并没有提供多大的实质性帮助。

根据公共租界"A"区和"B"区负责警官编制的统计数据，显而易见，自1941年1月7日开始的第八次销售以来，购买这种平价大米的人中，绝大部分并非公共租界居民。

"A"区记录显示租界居民占16.9%。
"B"区记录显示租界居民占40%。
"C"区记录显示租界居民占比极小。

法国警察也报告称，法租界内购买这种大米的大多数是非居民。

自上次平价大米销售于1941年1月7日开始至1941年1月15日（含），共有421,000人利用了此次销售机会，如前所述，其中大多数是公共租界或法租界的非居民，每日销售大米总量为1,500袋，其中较大部分流出租界，尽管有1938年7月7日发布的工部局通告第4976号，该通告要求将大米移出租界范围需经上海工部局警务处许可，发布该命令是为了保存租界内的大米库存。

（批注：秘书长兼总办 “特别许可出口”）
（印章：上海工部局总监办公室 1941年1月17日 3）

page_data.en:
-2-

In addition, the crowds gathering in order to take
advantage of this cheap sale are of such a nature that the
problem of keeping order is assuming major proportions, it
being necessary to post members of police at these shops,
which men can be ill spared from normal duties.

In view of the fact that the Shanghai Municipal Council
and the French Council Administration have each promised to
contribute a grant of $50,000 and $15,000 respectively in
order to finance the further sale of cheap rice, payable
over a period of three months, it is necessary if the
cheap sale of this rice is to be continued that some
arrangements should be made that only bona fide residents
of the Settlement should benefit.

It is practically impossible for the S.M. Police to
check or effect the registration of residents of the
Settlement who may wish to take advantage of this cheap
sale, therefore it is suggested that Mr. Yu Ya Ching
should attempt to devise some scheme with the assistance
of the various Chinese Guilds in order to ensure that the
cheap sale of rice is only available to residents of the
International and French Concession, failing which, in view
of the small proportion of residents of the Settlement who
benefit or the relief effected in alleviating the conditions
of bona fide residents of the Settlements these cheap sales
should be discontinued.

Officials of the Salvation Army would give Mr. Yu Ya
Ching any assistance that may be in their power but they are
afraid that they have not the necessary effective strength
to be of much assistance.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 16/1/41）
（印：...POLICE... JAN 22 1941 ...）
page_data.zh:
-2-

此外，为利用此次平价销售而聚集的人群性质使得维持秩序的问题变得日益严重，不得不在这些店铺部署警力，而这些人员原本难以从正常勤务中抽调。

鉴于上海工部局和法公董局已分别承诺拨款50,000美元和15,000美元，以资助为期三个月的进一步平价大米销售，如果要继续这种大米的平价销售，就必须做出某种安排，确保只有租界的真正居民才能受益。

上海工部局警务处实际上不可能核查或登记希望利用此次平价销售的租界居民，因此建议虞洽卿先生在各华人公会的协助下尝试制定某种方案，以确保大米平价销售仅适用于公共租界和法租界的居民，否则，鉴于受益的租界居民比例很小，或在缓解租界真正居民状况方面效果甚微，应停止这些平价销售。

救世军的官员将为虞洽卿先生提供力所能及的任何协助，但他们担心他们没有足够的有效人力来提供多大帮助。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特别处 1941年1月16日）
（印章：...警察... 1941年1月22日 ...）

Divisional Office "B" Division,
January 15th, 1941.

D.C. (Divisions)

Cheap Sale of Rice.

In "B" Division there are 22 shops engaged
in catering for the sale of cheap rice to poor
people. About half of these sell tickets and the
other half retail the rice.
The sale of tickets and rice takes place
between 1 p.m. and 5 p.m. daily. Crowds usually
start collecting during the early part of the
forenoon and police are posted between 10 and 11
a.m. until 5 p.m.. During the present sale of rice
the daily purchasers are far in excess of that
ever seen before and a check shows that roughly
60% of the people come from outside the Settlement.
Formerly two C.P.Cs. were usually sufficient
to cope with the queues at each shop but now at
many of them from three to six are required and
frequently squads from the station have to turn out
to restore order amongst the clamouring and unruly
hordes.
To control these crowds, 60% of whom are
non-residents of the Settlement, requires a large
number of police, particularly in Gordon Road and
Sinza districts where most of the shops are located,

致分区总监（各分区）

廉价大米销售事宜。

在“B”分区内，有22家店铺从事向穷人销售廉价大米的业务。其中约一半店铺出售票券，另一半则零售大米。
票券和大米的销售时间为每日下午1时至5时。人群通常在上午早些时候便开始聚集，警察于上午10时至11时之间上岗执勤，直至下午5时。在目前的大米销售期间，每日购买者人数远远超过以往任何时期，经核查显示，大约60%的人来自租界以外。
过去，每个店铺通常只需两名中国巡捕（C.P.Cs.）便足以应付排队人群，但现在许多店铺需要三至六名，且经常需要从警局调派小队出动，以在喧闹且不守秩序的人群中恢复秩序。
要控制这些其中有60%为非租界居民的人群，需要大量警力，尤其是在戈登路（Gordon Road）和静安寺（Sinza）地区，因为大多数店铺都位于此处，

page_data.en:
- 2 -

and at the present time with so many other
duties to fulfil, including barriers, guards
at residences, etc., the Division is, during
the daytime, very sparsely policed.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No. ..........
                                Gordon Road ....Station,
            REPORT              Date....January 9th, 41.

Subject: Control of Crowds at Rice Shops during Cheap Sales.

Made by XXX        and                Forwarded by....Inspector Trodd.

Sir,
    With reference to the above subject, I have to state
that between the hours of 1 p.m. - 5 p.m. on 8-1-41
thirty six C.P.C.s were withdrawn from regular beats and
posts in this District to control crowds purchasing cheap
rice.
    Nine shops were covered, approximately 14,000 coupons
sold, many persons being turned away.
    Even the posting of these C.P.C.s was insufficient,
barbed wire knife rests being used to prevent the crowds
from storming the shops. The use of knife rests is very
unsatisfactory there being always the possibility of
some one in the crowd either falling or being forced
against the wire and receiving an injury.
    The use of thirty six C.P.C.s on this particular duty
is a heavy drain on the Station staff and they can be ill
spared from other more important duties connected with
the suppression of crime. Few beats can be covered only
men for Traffic Posts, barriers, Extra-Settlement Roads
and special posts i.e. Judge houses etc., being available.
    I respectfully suggest that there are two possible
                            that
ways of ensuring/these shops are adequately covered by
Police.
    (1) Augmenting the Station staff and the forming of
        a special squad to cover them.
        This is a difficult proposition seeing that all
        districts are in the same position.
    (2) Reducing the number of shops selling coupons and
        rice.
        If this could be arranged less C.P.C.s would be
required, even though more prospective customers attend.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently
Trodd.
Officer i/c.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。    档案号 ..........
                                戈登路（Gordon Road）....警局，
            报告              日期....1941年1月9日。

主题：廉价销售期间大米店铺的人群控制。

由 XXX 制作                并由....特罗德（Trodd）巡官转呈。

先生，
    关于上述主题，本人须陈述，在1941年1月8日下午1时至5时之间，本区从常规巡逻路线和岗位上撤下了三十六名中国巡捕（C.P.Cs.），以控制购买廉价大米的人群。
    共覆盖了九家店铺，售出约14,000张票券，许多人被拒之门外。
    即使部署了这些中国巡捕仍显不足，不得不使用带刺铁丝网刀架来防止人群冲击店铺。使用刀架的效果非常令人不满，因为人群中总有人可能跌倒或被挤向铁丝网而受伤。
    将三十六名中国巡捕用于此项特定任务，对警局人员造成了沉重负担，使他们难以从其他与镇压犯罪有关的更重要职责中抽身。只有交通岗、路障、越界筑路区域（Extra-Settlement Roads）以及特殊岗位（即法官住宅等）的警力得以保留，常规巡逻路线几乎无法覆盖。
    本人谨建议有两种可能的
                            那
确保/这些店铺得到警方充分覆盖的方法。
    (1) 增加警局人员并组建一个专门小队来覆盖这些店铺。
        鉴于所有分区都处于相同境地，这是一个困难的提议。
    (2) 减少出售票券和大米的店铺数量。
        如果能如此安排，即使有更多潜在顾客前来，所需的中國巡捕也会减少。

此致，
敬礼
特罗德（Trodd）。
主管警官。

Sir,

With reference to the above subject, I beg to
report that there are seven shops in the Jinza
District dealing in cheap rice (three coupon shops

Each purchaser is allowed two tickets ($1-

The purchasers of such rice are of the
